title: How Persona Conditioning Changes Open-Ended Task Execution: A Paired Evaluation of Behavioral Gains and Reliability Costs
abstract: arXiv:2611.31264v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often prompted with role- or persona-based instructions, yet persona conditioning has mainly been evaluated through character fidelity or aggregate benchmark accuracy. We study persona conditioning as a task-execution steering signal that changes how models interpret, structure, and sustain responses. Using paired instances derived from real user role-play logs and expanded into simulated multi-turn continuations, we compare with-persona and no-persona conditions while fixing task content, constraints, user simulation, and evaluation criteria. Across eight models, persona conditioning improves expert content depth and procedural fidelity, and these gains survive length control. At the same time, it lowers strict instruction-following accuracy by 17 to 30 points in every model evaluated, and increases unsupported real-world specificity through persona-induced elaboration. translated_title: 人设条件化如何改变开放式任务执行：行为收益与可靠性成本的配对评估
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）经常通过角色或人设类指令进行提示，然而人设条件化此前主要通过角色忠实度或基准测试的总体准确率来评估。我们将人设条件化视为一种任务执行的引导信号，研究它如何改变模型解释、组织和维持回复的方式。基于从真实用户角色扮演日志中提取并扩展为模拟多轮对话延续的配对实例，我们在固定任务内容、约束条件、用户模拟和评估标准的前提下，比较了带人设与不带人设两种条件。在八个模型上的实验表明，人设条件化提升了专家内容深度和流程忠实度，且这些收益在长度控制后依然存在。与此同时，它在所有被评估的模型中将严格指令遵循准确率降低了17至30个百分点，并通过人设诱发的细节扩充增加了缺乏依据的现实世界具体描述。
tldr: 该论文通过配对实验首次系统揭示了人设条件化作为任务引导信号的双面性：它能提升LLM回复的专家内容深度和流程忠实度，但会以17至30个百分点的幅度降低严格指令遵循准确率并引发无依据的细节虚构。
en_tdlr: Through paired evaluation, this paper reveals the dual nature of persona conditioning as a steering signal: it improves content depth and procedural fidelity in open-ended tasks, but degrades strict instruction-following accuracy by 17-30 points and induces unsupported elaboration.
